To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) cognitive loading did not affect the participants' trajectory formation and trajectory deviations; (b) cognitive loading affected walking kinematics, in particularly walking velocity; and (c) cognitive loading impaired motor awareness in trials with high uncertainty.
cognitive loading affects motor control but not trajectory formation in goal directed walking in virtual reality environments.

the question of how cognitive load affects motor performance in a virtual reality environment.
the question how the central nervous system controls the execution of motor actions.
the effects of cognitive load and perceptual uncertainty on motor performance and motor awareness during locomotion.

cognitive load does not affect trajectory formation, but it does affect kinematics and motor awareness.
cognitive loading does not affect trajectory formation during walking in VR, although it does affect movement kinematics and motor awareness.

cognitive loading affects movement kinematics, but not trajectory formation, during goal directed locomotion.
the cognitive system is not involved in motor planning and control of goal directed walking, at least not to the extent that it is in other types of movements.
